subject: Algorithms
title: Discover Binary Search
description: Discover how Binary Search finds a value by repeatedly discarding half of a sorted list.

mission.title: Find the Hidden Number
mission.description: Use the middle value to narrow a sorted search area.

quiz.question: Why is Binary Search faster than checking every element?
options: It discards about half of the remaining values at each step.
It checks every value at the same time.
It only works with one number.

discovery.title: Halve the Search Area
discovery.summary: Binary Search compares the middle value, then removes the half that cannot contain the target.

sections.title: What is Binary Search?
sections.content: Binary Search finds a target by repeatedly checking the middle of a list.

sections.title: Why sorted matters
sections.content: The values must be sorted so a middle comparison tells us which half to discard.

sections.title: Using the middle
sections.content: If the target is larger, search the right half. If it is smaller, search the left half.

sections.title: Time complexity
sections.content: Binary Search runs in O(log n) time because the remaining search area is cut roughly in half each step.

sections.title: Simple example
sections.content: To find 60, compare it with 40 first. Since 60 is larger, discard the values up to 40 and check the new middle.

alternate_explanations.title: Think of finding a page
alternate_explanations.content: To find a page in a sorted book, open near the middle. The page number tells you whether to keep looking in the left or right half.

alternate_explanations.title: Find 60 step by step
alternate_explanations.content: In [10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70], check 40 first. Since 60 is larger, fade out 10 through 40. The new middle is 60, so it is found.

introduction.title: Meet Binary Search
introduction.content: Binary Search finds a value in a sorted list by checking the middle instead of checking every item one by one.
points: The middle comparison removes one impossible half.
You will watch the search area shrink.

worked_example.title: Find 60 by halving
worked_example.content: The middle value tells us which half could still contain the target.

steps.explanation: Values up to 40 cannot be 60, so the search keeps only the right half.
The new middle is 60, so the target is found.

worked_example.conclusion: Each comparison removes many values at once, which is why Binary Search is fast.

next.title: Search the array below.
next.content: Use the middle value and notice which values fade away.

action_explanations.check-middle: The middle value is the best comparison because it divides the remaining search area.
action_explanations.eliminate-half: The faded half cannot contain the target, so the search continues only where the target could be.
action_explanations.find-target: The target matches the current middle value, so the search is complete.

challenge.title: Binary Search Challenge
challenge.start_message: Find the target again by using the middle and discarding only impossible values.
challenge.continue_message: Challenge complete. Keep stepping through the sorted array to see the search reset.

phases.title: Find 60 efficiently
phases.instruction: Use the middle comparison, remove the impossible half, and reach the target.

target.label: Target
target.description: Find 60 while leaving the discarded half visibly faded.

phases.feedback: Use the middle comparison before deciding which half can be discarded.

recall.title: Recall
recall.prompt: In your own words, why must the values be sorted for Binary Search to work?
recall.empty_message: Write a short explanation before submitting.
recall.model_answer: Sorting makes a middle comparison meaningful: if the target is larger or smaller than the middle, an entire half is known to be impossible.

levels.label: Practice

guidance.start_message: Use the highlighted middle value to decide which half can still contain the target.

items.content: Compare 73 with the highlighted middle value. If the target is larger, keep the right half.

levels.operation_rule: Each middle comparison counts once. Declaring NOT FOUND after the search area is empty does not add a comparison.

phases.title: Find 73
phases.instruction: Decide what Binary Search should do after each middle comparison.
phases.feedback: Compare the target with the highlighted middle value before choosing a direction.

levels.label: Apply

guidance.start_message: Choose the search direction yourself. The array is still sorted, but Byte will not explain the comparison before you decide.

items.content: Only compare the target with the current middle. Do not use values that have already faded.

levels.operation_rule: Each middle comparison counts once. Declaring NOT FOUND after the search area is empty does not add a comparison.

phases.title: Find 22 with fewer prompts
phases.instruction: Keep narrowing the current search area until the target is the middle value.

target.label: Target
target.description: Find 22 without being told which half to choose.

phases.feedback: Recheck the target and current middle value before committing to a direction.

levels.label: Solve

guidance.start_message: This target is not guaranteed to be present. Keep searching until you have evidence that no candidates remain.

items.content: NOT FOUND is valid only after every remaining candidate has been eliminated.

levels.operation_rule: Each middle comparison counts once. Declaring NOT FOUND after the search area is empty does not add a comparison.

phases.title: Prove 73 is absent
phases.instruction: Search carefully. Choose NOT FOUND only once the current search area is empty.

target.label: Target
target.description: Determine whether 73 exists in the sorted array.

phases.feedback: There is still a possible candidate. Compare the target with the highlighted middle first.

levels.label: Mastery

guidance.start_message: This unfamiliar sorted array was generated for this attempt. Decide every step without hints.

levels.operation_rule: Each middle comparison counts once. Declaring NOT FOUND after the search area is empty does not add a comparison. No hints are available.

phases.title: Master an unfamiliar search
phases.instruction: Work from the current middle value until you correctly find the target or prove that it is absent.

target.label: Search challenge
target.description: The target may be present or absent.

phases.feedback: Use only the current middle comparison to choose the next step.

thinking.title: Think before you search
thinking.start_message: Mentally follow each middle comparison before the search is replayed.
thinking.instruction: Use the sorted starting array and target to predict Binary Search's comparison path.
thinking.do_not_execute: Do not make search decisions yet. Follow the comparisons mentally from top to bottom.

solve.title: Expert Search
solve.start_message: Choose every Binary Search decision yourself. The best comparison count remains hidden until you finish.
solve.instruction: Find the target or prove it absent. No path, next middle, or hints are revealed.
solve.operation_rule: Each middle comparison counts once. Declaring NOT FOUND after the search area is empty does not add a comparison.
solve.feedback: Compare the target with the current middle before deciding.
